findings.title: TRIGGER_CUSTOM_FIELD_SET triggerValue stored verbatim — no length cap, no format check on save
findings.description:
In applyTriggers (FunnelService.java:786), the TRIGGER_CUSTOM_FIELD_SET case is now: trigger.setTriggerValue(dto.triggerValue()); — entirely unvalidated on save. The pre-change code called requireFieldKeyValue which at minimum enforced non-blank. The new code stores an arbitrary-length, arbitrary-content string verbatim in MongoDB. The TriggerDto.triggerValue field carries no @Size annotation (confirmed: TriggerDto.java:33 has no constraint). At execution time (StepExecutor.java:430,438) this key flows into applyAll which uses it as a MongoDB dotted-path segment: update.set("customFields." + entry.getKey(), ...). A value containing a dot (e.g. "x.y") is a MongoDB operator/path injection vector. SubscriberCustomFieldsService.java:105 explicitly documents the precondition: 'every key MUST originate from a validated project field definition — a slug matching ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$ (no dots / Mongo-operator chars)' — but SET_CUSTOM_FIELD step validation deferred the non-blank presence check without adding an always-on format check for the step's customFieldKey field.

Note: this finding is about the TRIGGER_CUSTOM_FIELD_SET trigger type's triggerValue (the field key stored on the trigger, not the SET_CUSTOM_FIELD step). The step's customFieldKey (FunnelService.java:1145) is also stored verbatim from dto.customFieldKey() in toSteps and requireCustomFieldKey (presence check) is deferred to content=true. However, the step's customFieldKey goes through resolveFieldType/validateAndNormalize which will fail at execution for an unknown key — the trigger triggerValue is the higher-risk path because it directly reaches applyAll at execution time.
findings.impact: A draft save with triggerValue='x.$where' or 'x.y.z' (dotted path) persists to MongoDB. At execution time the key flows into update.set/unset as a MongoDB field path. MongoDB NoSQL injection via dotted-path operator chars (dot injection). Severity reduced from critical to major because the key must match a project CustomFieldDefinition before applyAll is reached (resolveFieldType returns null for unknown keys → StepResult.cont() skips the write), partially mitigating exploitation. However the value is still persisted without sanitisation, violating the SubscriberCustomFieldsService precondition.
findings.cwe: CWE-943 (Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic)

findings.title: Two null-valued TRIGGER_EVENT entries collapse to the same '' dedupe key, allowing two incomplete event triggers to persist on a draft save
findings.description: In applyTriggers (FunnelService.java:795), blank/null event triggerValues are normalised to '' for dedupe: `seenEventNames.add(eventName == null ? "" : eventName)`. Two TRIGGER_EVENT elements both with null/blank triggerValue each map to '' and the second will throw CODE_DUPLICATE_EVENT_NAME — this is working as documented. HOWEVER, the first one gets past the add() call and is stored, while the second is rejected. The issue is subtle: the dedupe semantics changed from 'two distinct event names must differ' to 'at most one incomplete (null/blank) event trigger is allowed at draft time.' This is intentional per the code comment but represents a semantic change that could confuse a user who adds two incomplete event triggers — the second is rejected not because event names must be present but because the empty key collides. This is a minor design issue / information accuracy problem, not a security vulnerability, but is worth noting for correctness.
findings.impact: Low. An author adding two draft event triggers both with no triggerValue gets a CODE_DUPLICATE_EVENT_NAME error, which is misleading (there is no actual event_name yet). No security impact.
findings.recommendation: Consider either (a) allowing multiple incomplete event triggers on draft (skip dedupe for null/blank values) and enforce uniqueness only for present values, or (b) document this as known UX friction in the tech-spec. Not a security blocker.

security_check_confirmations.customFieldKey_format_if_present: NOT CONFIRMED — see Finding 1 above. The TRIGGER_CUSTOM_FIELD_SET triggerValue and the SET_CUSTOM_FIELD step customFieldKey are stored verbatim on draft save with no always-on format guard. The slug pattern constraint is missing at save time.

security_check_confirmations.JsonIgnoreProperties_intact: CONFIRMED — UpdateFunnelRequest (@JsonIgnoreProperties line 25), FunnelStepDto (line 27), TriggerDto (line 30), NoteDto (line 18), CanvasPositionDto (line 22) all carry @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true).

security_check_confirmations.SUBSCRIBE_TO_FUNNEL_target_validation: CONFIRMED ON SAVE (content=true path) — validateSubscribeTarget (FunnelService.java:1496-1508) called from the content=true switch case. This is correctly classified as content-completeness (targetFunnelId required), NOT a security check, so deferral to activate is acceptable.

summary: 1 major finding, 1 minor finding. The critical deferral boundary is correctly drawn: ONLY content-completeness (required-field presence) is deferred to activate(). Every structural/DoS/authz/injection guard runs on every save (content=false) — with ONE exception: TRIGGER_CUSTOM_FIELD_SET.triggerValue and SET_CUSTOM_FIELD step's customFieldKey are stored verbatim without an always-on format/slug check. For the trigger, this contradicts the SubscriberCustomFieldsService precondition (slug ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,32}$ required, no dots) and creates a latent MongoDB field-path injection vector. All other checked security properties — coordinates finite, MAX_TRIGGERS, on_start entryStepId funnel-scoped, tagSlug/eventName format-if-present, keyword caps, step count cap, UNKNOWN-type reject, note caps, server-minted ids, @JsonIgnoreProperties, requireFunnel ownership — CONFIRMED ON SAVE. verdict=fail due to the missing format-if-present guard on the custom_field_set trigger value.
